Olympus Water and Theme Park Resort''' is a [[theme park]] and [[water park]] resort complex in [[Wisconsin Dells, Wisconsin]]. The resort is themed after [[Ancient Greece]], particularly its [[Greek mythology|mythology]] and [[List of Greek deities|gods]], and is named after [[Mount Olympus|the mountain in Greece]] where those gods were said to live. Mount. Olympus features an indoor and outdoor water park (home to America's first rotating waterslide and America's tallest waterslide) and amusement park rides, and the complex includes dozens of [[mom-and-pop]] motel buildings that were acquired by the resort in addition to its purpose-built hotel (Hotel Rome). ==History== [[File:Mt.OlympusWater&ThemeParkEntrance.jpg|thumb|right|Park entrance]] ===Beginnings=== Mt. Olympus was started by the Laskaris family. Demetrios “Jim” Laskaris was born in [[Katsaros]], Greece and immigrated to the United States at the age of 13. He received a technical degree in Michigan, served for four years in the [[U.S. Navy]], and then owned and operated several restaurants in Chicago. The family moved to Wisconsin Dells, where Jim and his wife Fotoula opened a hot dog stand in 1970, which they named “Big Chief”, after a statue purchased from a trade show. The hot dog stand was a commercial failure, and the Laskaris family was nearly forced to return to Chicago. At the last minute, they found $700 in savings inside a sock, which they invested in a three-wheeler dirt track.{{cite web|url=https://www.mayoclinic.org/giving-to-mayo-clinic/philanthropy-in-action/features-stories/nick-and-eva-laskaris|title=Nick and Eva Laskaris: The king of Mt. Olympus helps find a new path for cancer treatment|website=[[Mayo Clinic]]}} The family expanded on their property by building a 7-unit motel, and in 1975 they added a [[go-kart]] track, "Goofy Karts", along the Wisconsin Dells Parkway. Nick Laskaris, Jim and Fotoula's son, became the go-karts' chief mechanic at the age of 9. Between 1978 & 1982, the family's business ventures continued as they opened a campground, [[trailer park|trailer court]], and began running country-western and Native American ceremony shows. When the lease on the go-kart track ran out in 1980, “Goofy Karts” was abandoned and a new cloverleaf track was built next to the Big Chief hot dog stand. It was also at this location that Nick Laskaris started constructing his own go-karts a few years later. Nick Laskaris became involved in the design and engineering of the various go-kart tracks on the property, which included the only multi-level go-kart tracks in the world. Big Chief Go-Kart World, as it was then known, developed new techniques for elevated go-kart tracks, which have now become standard. The family purchased several acres along the Wisconsin Dells Parkway, commonly known as the "Strip", and continued the park's expansion. In 1995, the park added the first [[roller coaster]] in the Wisconsin Dells, [[Cyclops (roller coaster)|Cyclops]], and changed its name to Big Chief Karts & Coasters. Another roller coaster, [[Pegasus (Mt. Olympus Water and Theme Park)|Pegasus]], was added the following year and [[Zeus (roller coaster)|Zeus]] opened in 1997. The park acquired Crazy King Ludwig's Adventure Park, which featured its own go-kart track, in 1999. This purchase brought Big Chief's to a total area of 107 acres. ===Mt. Olympus Water and Theme Park=== [[Image:WisconsinDellsWisconsinRollercoaster.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Hades 360 (then known as simply Hades) at Mt. Olympus, which has the world's longest underground tunnel on a roller coaster. The pictured section of the ride has since been modified to include a barrel roll and an overbanked turn.]] Big Chief Karts and Coasters was renamed to Big Chief's Mt. Olympus Theme Park in 2004 and the park expanded its Greco-Roman theming. Later that year, Mt. Olympus entered into a partnership with the Mattei family, owners of the nearby Treasure Island Resort. This partnership merged Treasure Island's outdoor Family Land Waterpark and the Bay of Dreams [[indoor water park]] with the Mt. Olympus theme park, creating a co-owned complex known as the ''Mt. Olympus Water and Theme Park''. These two parks were not physically connected at the time of the merger because the Playday Motel separated them, leading Mt. Olympus to purchase the Playday Motel and demolish it.{{cite web|url=http://www.jsonline.com/story/index.aspx?id=268554|title=Three Dells attractions become one theme park|author=Rick Romell|work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]|date=October 21, 2004|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070929121937/http://www.jsonline.com/story/index.aspx?id=268554|archive-date=2007-09-29}} The park opened their largest roller coaster, [[Hades 360|Hades]], for the 2005 season. Hades is a [[wooden roller coaster]] which became notable for its unusually steep drops and angles, and received the inaugural [[Golden Ticket Award for Best New Ride]] from ''[[Amusement Today]]'' magazine. This ride also goes upside down. In 2006, Mt. Olympus introduced the Parthenon Indoor Theme Park, a 43,000 sq ft building containing several amusement rides, including a spinning [[Wild Mouse roller coaster]] called Opa.{{cite web|url=http://www.wiscnews.com/wisconsindellsevents/news/local/article_862f33bb-f6ec-5286-b93d-96b87aea3df4.html|title=Indoor amusements to open|date=October 26, 2005|publisher=Wisconsin Dells Events}}{{cite RCDB|coaster_name=Opa|location=Mt. Olympus Water & Theme Park|rcdb_number=3386|accessdate=June 24, 2020}} dus acquired Treasure Island entirely from the Mattei family. The purchase also included Pleasant View Motel, which became "Mykonos Village", and the Captain's Quarters, a family-oriented hotel building which was sold to [[Bluegreen]] Resorts and now operates as "Bluegreen Odyssey Dells", attached to the Hotel Rome (formerly the Treasure Island Resort). With the acquisition from the Mattei family, Mt. Olympus added {{convert|60|acre|m2}} of real estate to their property, bringing the total area to {{convert|156|acre|km2|1}}.{{cite web|url=https://www.bizjournals.com/milwaukee/stories/2007/03/26/daily3.html|title=Mt. Olympus owners buy Treasure Island resort|author=Rick Romell|work=[[Milwaukee Business Journal]]|date=March 26, 2007}} The Lost City of Atlantis, a three-acre outdoor water park area, opened in 2012. Atlantis features seven new slides from [[WhiteWater West]], a monster dump bucket and a 120' [[geyser]], built at a cost of $3.5 million.{{cite web|url=http://www.wiscnews.com/wisconsindellsevents/news/local/article_9b340f9a-543b-11e1-990c-0019bb2963f4.html|title=Mt. Olympus to re-create Lost City of Atlantis|date=February 10, 2012|author=Hayden Marx|publisher=Wisconsin Dells Events}} Hades received a major renovation in 2013, adding a 360-degree inversion and the coaster was renamed [[Hades 360]].{{cite web|url=http://www.wiscnews.com/wisconsindellsevents/news/local/environment/article_0c9a86da-59d8-11e2-bafb-001a4bcf887a.html|title=Laskaris adds looping coaster|date=January 8, 2013|author=Norm Gibb|publisher=Wisconsin Dells Events}} "The Manticore", a vertical [[swing ride]], was added to the park in 2015.{{cite tweet|user=mtolympuspark|author=Mt. Olympus Resorts|number=617308098919727104|date=July 4, 2015|title=New for 2015 at Mt. Olympus — The Manticore}}{{cite web|url=http://www.wiscnews.com/wisconsindellsevents/news/local/article_76fdba2f-a86e-5a48-a5cc-dd03e7269eee.html|title=Manticore to swing at Mt. Olympus|date=January 21, 2015|author=Jackie Sonneberg|publisher=Wisconsin Dells Events}} "The Great Pool of Delphi", a 27,000 square foot swimming pool containing 500,000 gallons of water, was added in 2016. The pool was advertised as the largest swimming pool in Wisconsin Dells, the "waterpark capital of the world". The cost of this addition was $4 million.{{cite web|url=http://www.wiscnews.com/wisconsindellsevents/news/local/article_90a6459e-4ec2-5506-b013-610b25b7748a.html|title=Mt. Olympus adds 'Great Pool,' local residents get free summer passes|date=April 19, 2016|first=Ed|last=Legge|publisher=Wisconsin Dells Events}}{{cite web|url=http://www.wiscnews.com/portagedailyregister/business/article_7779e421-503d-517d-a985-4ee212b48f7d.html|title=Mt. Olympus in Wisconsin Dells adding massive pool|date=April 19, 2016|author=Barry Adams|publisher=Wisconsin Dells Events}} In 2019, Mount Olympus representatives announced at the [[International Association of Amusement Parks and Attractions|IAAPA Expo]] their purchase of a new Slidewheel waterslide for the 2021 season.{{cite web|url=https://www.ramaker.com/company-news/ramaker-associates-to-engineer-the-installation-of-the-first-slidewheel-in-the-united-states/|title=Ramaker & Associates to Engineer the Installation of the First SlideWheel in the United States|date=December 3, 2019|website=www.ramaker.com|access-date=August 9, 2021}} Tentatively named ''Hercules'', the slide would consist of a [[Perpetual motion|perpetually rotating]] wheel in which rafts would be dispatched into every 30 seconds, and move through the knot of slide tunnels akin to a massive [[hamster wheel]].{{cite web|url=https://www.parkerlebnis.de/mt-olympus-erstes-slidewheel-in-amerika-ankuendigung_105298.html|title=Mt. Olympus baut erstes SlideWheel in Amerika: Neuartige Wasserrutsche kommt in die Staaten|date=December 10, 2019|author=Alexander Louis|website=www.parkerlebnis.de|access-date=August 9, 2021|language=german}} However, the impact of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] in 2020 halted plans to install the slide in time for the 2021 season. The renamed Medusa's Slidewheel{{Cite web |title=America's First Slidewheel |url=https://www.mtolympuspark.com/specials/americas-first-coming-in-2022/ |access-date=2022-05-12 |website=Mt. Olympus Water & Theme Park |language=en}} was formally announced on August 6, 2021, and opened within the Indoor Waterpark area for the 2022 season.{{Cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/mtolympuspark/videos/535398937791655/|title=Mt. Olympus Resorts & Parks|date=August 6, 2021|website=[[Facebook]]|language=en|access-date=August 9, 2021}} The Slidewheel's addition also brought about an expansion to the indoor waterpark, with a general pool named Serpent's Pool.{{Cite web |title=2022 Park Map |url=https://www.mtolympuspark.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/park-map-2022-new-scaled.jpg}} In 2024, Mount Olympus opened ''The Rise of'' ''Icarus'' waterslide complex, which includes the ''Icarus Tower (''consisting of 5 slides, ''The Journey, The Drop, The Voyage, The Flight,'' and ''The Fall'', the tallest [[water slide]] in the United States) {{Cite web |last=Groebner |first=Simon Peter |date=2024-06-21 |title=America's new tallest waterslide is in Wisconsin Dells. Here's what it's like to ride it. |url=https://www.startribune.com/tallest-waterslide-wisconsin-dells-rise-of-icarus-minnesota-midwest-mt-olympus-waterparks/600375117 |access-date=2025-04-04 |website=www.startribune.com |language=en}} and the ''Icaria Splash 'N Slide'', a new children's waterplay area. At 145 feet tall, ''The Rise of Icarus'' broke both records for North America's tallest waterslide, against the indoor slides ''Thrillagascar and Jungle Jammer'' (142 feet) at [[DreamWorks Water Park]] in New Jersey; and against the outdoor slide complex ''Daredevil's Peak'' (135 feet) at [[CocoCay]].{{Cite web |last=Levine |first=Arthur |title=America's tallest water slide to rise in Wisconsin |url=https://www.aboutthemeparks.fun/p/americas-tallest-water-slide-to-rise |access-date=2025-04-04 |website=www.aboutthemeparks.fun |language=en}} ===Acquisitions of other properties=== In 2010 and 2011, the park purchased several smaller nearby independent motels and hotels and renamed them, creating seven new lodging areas and painting the buildings blue and white to fit the Greek theme.{{cite web|url=http://www.wiscnews.com/wisconsindellsevents/news/local/article_bd012d6c-1ad7-11e1-86dc-001cc4c002e0.html|title=Laskaris buys Copa Cabana|author=Anna Krejci|date=29 November 2011 |publisher=Wisconsin Dells Events}} These acquisitions included the Star Motel{{cite web|url=http://www.wiscnews.com/wisconsindellsevents/news/local/article_89a85d0a-e39c-11df-9030-001cc4c03286.html|title=Laskaris buys Star motels, buffet on Strip|author=Andy Steinke|date=29 October 2010 |publisher=Wisconsin Dells Events}} and Luna Inn & Suites (which became Poseidon's Village),{{cite web|url=http://www.wiscnews.com/wisconsindellsevents/news/local/article_47c3ccaa-1450-11e0-83d7-001cc4c03286.html|title=Laskaris buys 2 motels|date=Dec 30, 2010|author=Andy Steinke|publisher=Wisconsin Dells Events}} the Riverwalk Hotel (which became Santorini Village),{{cite web|url=http://www.wiscnews.com/wisconsindellsevents/news/local/article_f9395ee4-2b27-11e0-8db2-001cc4c002e0.html|title=Laskarises buy Riverwalk, American World|date=Jan 28, 2011|author=Andy Steinke|publisher=Wisconsin Dells Events}} American World Resort & Campground (which became Zeus's Village), and the Four Seasons Motel (which became Poseidon's Village). Mt. Olympus also purchased the Raintree Resort and Conference Center, the first hotel built by Todd Nelson, who currently owns the [[Kalahari Resort]].{{cite web|url=http://www.wiscnews.com/wisconsindellsevents/news/local/article_25139de8-2026-11e0-bdd1-001cc4c002e0.html|title=Laskaris buys Raintree|date=January 4, 2011|author=Andy Steinke|publisher=Wisconsin Dells Events}} The Copa Cabana Resort Hotel & Suite was completely renovated after it was purchased by Mt. Olympus in 2011, and it reopened as the core of "Mt. Olympus Village" the following spring. All of the resort's acquired motels were rebranded once again to Mt. Olympus Village in 2013.{{cite web|url=http://www.wiscnews.com/wisconsindellsevents/news/local/crime_and_courts/article_ca545120-d2e0-11e2-b20a-0019bb2963f4.html|title=Mt. Olympus acquires another motel on Strip|date=June 11, 2013|author=Anna Krejci|publisher=Wisconsin Dells Events}} This change coincided with the purchases of the Concord Inn and the Monaco Motel. The addition of these properties gave the resort a total of over 1,300 rooms.{{cite web|url=http://www.wiscnews.com/wisconsindellsevents/news/local/article_5f4e64ea-dc79-50ce-a524-f0952b87bbb4.html |title=Resort takes over more motels|date=October 24, 2013|author=Anna Krejci|publisher=Wisconsin Dells Events}} Recent acquisitions include the Diamond Hotel in 2015 and the Ambers Resort and Conference Center in 2016.{{cite web|url=https://www.mtolympuspark.com/wisconsin-dells-diamond-hotel|title=Lodging — Mt. Olympus|website=Mt. Olympus}} ===Incidents=== On March 6, 2014, a lap bar malfunction caused by inadequate maintenance occurred on the Opa roller coaster in the indoor theme park, causing a 63-year-old man from [[Fremont, Wisconsin]], to fall 17 feet from the ride, sustaining serious injuries that left him in a coma for three weeks. The ride was permanently closed following the incident and later removed.{{cite web|url=http://www.wiscnews.com/wisconsindellsevents/news/local/article_c8fa5bbb-2e1d-5ea8-a2d1-a0698f973f5e.html|title=Coaster accident witnesses say lap bar was not secure|date=March 28, 2014|author=Kay James|publisher=Wisconsin Dells Events}}{{cite web|url=http://www.wiscnews.com/wisconsindellsevents/news/local/article_e9745da3-a833-5f39-ac46-cf596f3708a9.html|title=State finds violations at Mt. Olympus in coaster accident|author=Kay James|date=April 2, 2014|publisher=Wisconsin Dells Events}}{{cite web|url=https://www.greenbaypressgazette.com/story/news/2016/08/18/wisconsin-amusement-rides-lack-tracking-enforcement/88864774/|title=2 killed, 75 hurt on Wis. rides since '06|date=August 18, 2016|author=Eric Litke|work=[[Green Bay Press-Gazette]]}} On January 23, 2015, a 4-year-old nearly drowned in the indoor water park. EMS responded and took the child to St. Clair Hospital. Three months after the incident, the Dells-Delton EMS team presented Mt. Olympus and the lifeguards involved in rescuing the child with certificates for life-saving efforts.{{cite web|url=http://www.wiscnews.com/wisconsindellsevents/news/local/article_e8af8ca8-7434-523b-a5ad-894fef4cc791.html|title=Mt. Olympus lifeguards recognized for heroics|date=April 24, 2015|first=Ed|last=Legge|publisher=Wisconsin Dells Events}}{{cite web|url=http://www.wiscnews.com/wisconsindellsevents/news/local/article_ca6e3120-b8d3-5332-a291-07f199bb982a.html|title=4-year-old nearly drowns at Mt. Olympus|date=January 23, 2015|author=Jason Cuevas|publisher=Wisconsin Dells Events}} In July 2015, an elastic cable snapped on "The Catapult" [[reverse bungee]] ride located in the outdoor theme park. A video of the incident was uploaded to [[Facebook]] and was widely shared before ultimately being removed. The ride was owned and operated by Casco, Inc., and was an up-charge attraction that was not included with the price of admission to the park. Mt. Olympus removed the ride from the park two days later.{{cite web|url=http://www.wiscnews.com/wisconsindellsevents/news/local/article_06e16798-cd0f-5c8e-bc81-2837e6b0bb85.html|title=Near miss at Mt. Olympus lights up Facebook|date=July 9, 2015|first=Ed|last=Legge|publisher=Wisconsin Dells Events}}{{cite web|url=http://www.wiscnews.com/wisconsindellsevents/news/article_c86f0839-3b0d-55e2-bd1b-5b532eb95311.html|title=Mt. Olympus removes thrill ride after close call|date=July 10, 2015|first=Ed|last=Legge|publisher=Wisconsin Dells Events}}{{cite web|url=http://www.wiscnews.com/portagedailyregister/news/local/article_487fb5be-ebd9-52b2-b373-eb3832f649e1.html|title=Ride's owner cited in past for violations in Dells|date=July 10, 2015|author=Rob Schultz|publisher=Wisconsin Dells Events}}{{cite web|url=http://www.wiscnews.com/baraboonewsrepublic/news/local/article_0d8e845a-24d2-5408-8b17-4cb928d990d3.html|title=State won't investigate failed thrill ride incident at Mt. Olympus|date=July 29, 2015|author=Rob Schultz|publisher=Wisconsin Dells Events}} ===Timeline=== *'''1995''': Addition of ''Cyclops'' wooden roller coaster *'''1996''': Addition of ''Pegasus'' wooden roller coaster *'''1997''': Additions of ''Zeus'' wooden roller coaster ''The Trojan Horse'' go-kart track *'''2000''': Addition of ''Kiddie Land'' *'''2004''': Addition of ''Dive to Atlantis'' water roller coaster.{{cite web|url=http://www.wiscnews.com/wisconsindellsevents/news/local/article_ee58deab-e66a-5866-b3f9-43e46aeb8db0.html|title=Big Chief expands|date=January 21, 2004|publisher=Wisconsin Dells Events}} *'''2005''': Additions of ''Hades'' wooden roller coaster and ''Triton's Water slide Tower'' *'''2006''': Additions of ''The Parthenon Indoor Theme Park'' and ''Thunder and Lightning Speed Slides'' *'''2007''': Additions of ''Poseidon's Rage Surf Pool'', ''Apollo's Swing'', ''Medusa's Indoor Waterpark'', "Neptune's outdoor water park'', ''Hotel Rome" and ''Mykonos Village''. ''Dive to Atlantis'' removed. *'''2008''': Addition of ''The River Troy'' *'''2009''': Additions of ''The Almighty Hermes'' Sky coaster and ''Night at the Theme Park'' *'''2010''': Additions of ''Catapult Extreme Ride'' and ''Poseidon's Beach'' *'''2011''': Additions of ''Poseidon's Village'', ''Zeus's Village'', ''Mykonos Resort'' and ''Santorini Village'' *'''2012''': Additions of ''Lost City of Atlantis'' water play structure and ''Mt. Olympus Village'' *'''2013''': ''Hades'' renovated & renamed ''Hades 360'', additions of ''Concord Inn'', ''Monaco Motel'' and ''Pine Dell Motel'' *'''2014''': ''Opa'' removed *'''2015''': Additions of ''The Manticore'' vertical swing ride, ''Diamond Hotel'' and ''Bridge View Motel''. Was branded '''Poseidon Underwater Go-Kart Track''' prior to 2018. |} ===Other rides=== * '''Apollo's Swing''' – A {{convert|100|ft|m|-1|adj=on}} [[S&S Power|S&S Sansei]] [[Screamin' Swing]] up-charge attraction that seats four passengers and reaches speeds of {{convert|70|mi/h|km/h|0|abbr=on}} * '''Batting Cages''' – 25 cent coin-operated machines * '''Kiddie Swing''' – A rotating circle of arms holding a swing in each, designed for children. * '''Kiddie Train''' – A children's train * '''Rock Wall''' – A 30-foot up-charge climbing wall * '''The Manticore''' – A 140-foot tall tower with a rotating center with 12 connected arms and 12 double-seat chairs, which can accommodate 24 guests, spinning them high in the air. ===Former rides=== * '''Catapult''' – A [[reverse bungee]] ride removed in July 2015 due to a cable snapping before two riders were launched into the air.{{cite web|url=http://www.nbc15.com/home/headlines/Ride-breaks-at-Mt-Olympus-313101891.html|title=UPDATE: State won't investigate failure of theme park ride|first=Lindsey|last=Branwall|website=[[WMTV|www.nbc15.com]]}} * '''Pan's Animal Farm''' – A Petting Zoo that allowed children to feed animals. * '''Dive to Atlantis''' – Opened in 2004 and 2007; E&F Miler [[Water coaster (roller coaster)|water coaster]] * '''The Almighty Hermes''' – A [[Skycoaster]] attraction that reaches heights of 100 feet and speeds of up to 45 miles per hour. ==Outdoor water park== ===Water slides=== [[Image:TritonWaterSlideEntranceMt.OlympusWater&ThemePark.jpg|thumb|right|Triton entrance]] *'''The Rise of Icarus''' – Opened in summer 2024, The Rise of Icarus broke the record for the tallest waterslide in America at 145 feet tall.{{cite web|url=https://www.cbs58.com/news/americas-tallest-waterslide-is-coming-to-mt-olympus-in-the-wisconsin-dells#:~:text=Olympus%20announced%2C%20%22The%20Rise%20of,slides%20and%20water%20play%20features. |title=America's tallest waterslide is coming to Mt. Keep an eye out for more details! . . #wisconsindells #wisdells #mtolympuspark #newattraction #summer2022 #americasfirst #summer #themepark" }} ==Indoor theme park == [[Image:TheParthenonMtOlympusWater&ThemePark.jpg|thumb|The outside exterior of the indoor theme park; the columns are made out of [[styrofoam]].]] ===Current rides=== * '''Balloon Ride''' * '''Bumper Cars''' * '''Crazy Trolley''' * '''Rock Wall Climb''' * '''Spring Ride''' * '''Tea Cups''' * '''The Arcade''' ===Former rides=== * '''Go-Karts''' * '''Disk'o''' * '''Free Fall''' * '''Opa''' ==Indoor water park== [[Image:IndoorWaterParkMt.OlympusWater&ThemePark.jpg|thumb|The side of the indoor waterpark building]] Medusa's Indoor Waterpark is a {{convert|60000|sqft|m2|-2|adj=on}} [[indoor water park]] at Mt. Olympus. It was originally part of the Treasure Island Resort and was available exclusively to Treasure Island guests before the merger with Mt. Olympus. When originally acquired it was called Bay of Dreams until the area was remodeled and expanded in 2021/2022. ===Water slides=== * '''Cerberus Tube Slide''' – Tube slide that is over 10 stories high * '''Hydra Body Slide''' – Basic body slide * '''Medusa's Shipwreck''' – A children's area with a {{convert|35|ft|m|1|adj=on}} long pirate ship complete with tattered sails, tunnels, five water slides, waterspouts and many geysers * '''Medusa's Slidewheel''' – A [[WhiteWater West]] SlideWheel attraction, opened in 2022 as the first of its kind in North America. ===Other attractions=== * '''The Fire Pool''' — hot tub * '''River Styx''' – lazy river * '''Scylla's Pool''' — whirlpool * '''Divine Warming Pool''' – simple pool area with soothing waters and calming sounds * '''Serpent's Pool''' — kid-friendly water play area ===Former rides=== * '''Cobra''' – Enclosed body slide, removed for the Slidewheel * '''Diamondback''' – Body slide, removed for the Slidewheel ==Night at the Theme Park== In the summer of 2009, Mt. Olympus began ''Night at the Theme Park'', where select rides (Hades 360, Poseidon's Rage, Zeus, Trojan Horse Go-Kart Track, Underworld Go-Kart Track and the Kiddie Land Rides) would be open from 10 pm to 1 am for four nights weekly. People who would attend would receive free soda and parking. Nick Laskaris got the idea when he took his children to go see [[Night at the Museum: Battle of the Smithsonian]] at the local cinema.{{cite web|url=http://www.wiscnews.com/wde/news/458324|title=7/15/2009 Park asks for late nights|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090829220349/http://www.wiscnews.com/wde/news/458324|archivedate=2009-08-29}} The village of Lake Delton did not approve the event, because it was in violation of its amusement ordinance in which businesses have to close around midnight and their 11 pm curfew law. Village trustees were worried about someone crossing the busy [[Wisconsin Dells Parkway]] at night and getting hit by a car.{{cite web|url=http://www.wiscnews.com/wde/news/459955|title=7/29/2009 Mt. Olympus continues night openings|publisher=}}{{dead link|date=February 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} The village of Lake Delton subsequently made some changes to the amusement ordinance, with a variance for businesses if they requested, including Mt. Olympus. extract: Mt. Olympus Water and Theme Park Resort is a theme park and water park resort complex in Wisconsin Dells, Wisconsin. The resort is themed after Ancient Greece, particularly its mythology and gods, and is named after the mountain in Greece where those gods were said to live. Mount. Olympus features an indoor and outdoor water park (home to America's first rotating waterslide and America's tallest waterslide) and amusement park rides, and the complex includes dozens of mom-and-pop motel buildings that were acquired by the resort in addition to its purpose-built hotel (Hotel Rome).
